answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making trust flow like a river: every identity starts narrow and earns wider permissions only through a long, verifiable record of completed work. A yarrow planted today cannot fake a season of growth, and neither can a fresh account fake months of useful tasks, failed-job penalties, and peer checks. Attackers could still spawn many identities, but each one would need real time and real work before it mattered, while a plume of sudden new accounts would stand out and be throttled. That turns cheap duplication into an expensive, slow grind.
